title: KV fragmentation policy & surge‑proof TTL synthesis with staged rollforward
creator: Alyssa Gomez
description: Design and implement a policy and automated pipeline that synthesizes per-prefix/kv TTLs, canonicalizes cache keys to reduce fragmentation, and applies changes via a staged rollforward with safety gates. The goal is to reduce token cost by increasing effective cache hit-rate without increasing tail latency or error rates. This ticket covers modeling, tooling to generate safe TTL suggestions, a canary/staged apply flow, and rollback automation hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Automated sampler produces per-prefix hit-rate and inter-arrival time (IAT) distribution for prefixes across 7 days
TTL suggestion engine emits a ranked TTL proposal CSV with confidence scores and expected hit-rate delta per prefix
Key canonicalizer ruleset reduces unique key cardinality for targeted prefixes by >= 18% in staging
Staged rollforward harness applies TTL changes to 1%, 10%, 50% traffic cohorts and will auto-rollback on defined violations
Runbook documented and validated with SOC/Oncall; rollout takes <48h to revert if triggered
rollout_plan: 1) Data collection: enable 72h high-granularity sampling (1m buckets) for candidate prefixes in staging (owner: data-pipeline)
2) Modeling: run hit-rate + IAT synthesis notebook (notebook link) to generate TTL candidates and confidence intervals
3) Pre-apply checks: static safety gate (min hit-rate lift >0.5%), cost delta estimate, and collision check for canonicalizer
4) Canary apply: 1% traffic for 24h with shadow replay for 100% traffic to compare hit-rate and latency metrics
5) Ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% over 72h if no safety triggers are fired
6) Full apply and continuous monitoring with 7-day watch window
rollback_plan: Auto-rollback triggers: p99 latency increase >15ms vs baseline OR error rate increase >0.25% OR cache hit-rate drop >5 percentage points
Immediate rollback: revert TTLs to previous values via stored config snapshot; disable canonicalizer for affected prefixes
Post-rollback diagnostics: collect sample traces, top-100 affected user keys, and run replay tests to reproduce regression
Manual approval path: if auto-rollback does not complete, page oncall and escalate to runtime leads
metrics_and_alerts: Primary metrics: prefix-level cache hit-rate, effective token cost per 1k requests, p50/p95/p99 latency for generation endpoint
Safety metrics: 5m rolling error rate, allocation queue depth, inference GPU utilization
Alert rules: TTL-APPLY-ERRRATE (>=0.25% for 10m), TTL-APPLY-P99-LAT (>=15ms increase for 5m), TTL-APPLY-HITDROPPCT (>=5pt drop for 15m)
modeling_approach: Sampling: stratified sampling by customer cohort and prefix frequency to avoid bias from heavy hitters
Hit-rate model: Poisson arrival + exponential IAT fit per prefix to estimate marginal benefits of TTL change
Cost projection: simulate cache behavior using discrete-event simulator (existing cache-simulator binary) with candidate TTLs and canonicalization rules
Uncertainty: Monte Carlo over 1000 draws to estimate 90% confidence interval for hit-rate lift and cost savings
canonicalization_rules: Strip session and ephemeral numeric suffixes (regex list maintained in repo)
Collapse user-id tokens into stable hashed prefix when safe (opt-in per prefix via labeling)
Preserve semantic tokens (model-internal prompt markers) to avoid over-canonicalizing and causing collisions
safety_gates: Collision guard: simulated collision rate <0.1% in staging for proposed canonicalizer rules
Max per-prefix eviction risk: projected increased eviction for other prefixes <2%
Traffic shaping: do not apply TTLs that would increase hot-spot load on a single shard above configured shard_threshold
Human checkpoint: final apply to >50% requires sign-off from runtime PM and one engineering lead
notes_and_decisions: Decided to prefer conservative TTL increases (+10-30%) for low-confidence prefixes rather than aggressive changes
Will separate key-canonicalizer rollout from TTL changes where collision risk is moderate to isolate impact
Use existing cache-simulator; we added per-prefix eviction heatmap output in PR #1247
We will not canonicalize PII-like prefixes (customer-configurable exemption list)
